pr_title: GDScript: Don't warn on unassigned for builtin-typed variables
pr_body:
If the type of a variable is a built-in Variant type, then it will automatically be assigned a default value based on the type. This means that the explicit initialization may be unnecessary. Thus, this commit removes the warning in such case.

This also changes the meaning of the unassigned warning to happen when the variable is used before being assigned, not when it has zero assignments.

Fix #85796
Fix #88117
pr_comments: It technically does break compatibility, but I don't think it's a big deal in this case. The warning will now help catch more potential errors (by checking use before assignment, not only missing assignment) while being more lenient with built-in types which already have a sane default.

issue_context.title: Local scope variable generates error 'The variable "a"  was used but never assigned a value.'
issue_context.body:
### Tested versions

Godot v4.2.1.stable 
Godot v4.2.stable 

Does not compile in V3.5.3

### System information

- Fedora Linux 39 (Workstation Edition) - Wayland - Vulkan (Mobile) - integrated Intel(R) HD Graphics 530 (SKL GT2) () - Intel(R) Core(TM) i5-6500 CPU @ 3.20GHz (4 Threads)

### Issue description

The following generates the error:
```
extends Node
func _ready():
	var a: Array[int]
	a.resize(16)
	a.fill(0)
	for i in range(16):
		a[i] = i*2
	print(a)
```

However, moving the array declaration out of the local scope  generates no errors:

```
extends Node
var a: Array[int]
func _ready():
	a.resize(16)
	a.fill(0)
	for i in range(16):
		a[i] = i*2
	print(a)
```


### Steps to reproduce

Write single node app with the above code and run  both versions.

### Minimal reproduction project (MRP)

[array_fill_bug.zip](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/files/14214692/array_fill_bug.zip)
comments:
It's not an error, just one of the many superfluous warnings ;),
IIRC there was a bug report about it somewhere.

You can disable it with
```go
@warning_ignore("unassigned_variable")
var a: Array[int]

or use
var a: Array[int] = []
```

or global in the project settings

![image](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/assets/4047289/80bd7287-2319-4390-b24c-b4eb68deadfb)
In a nutshell, the broader issue here is that methods that directly operate on the declared **Variant** do not count towards the variable being "used".

> In a nutshell, the broader issue here is that methods that directly operate on the declared **Variant** do not count towards the variable being "used".

No, that is not an issue. Those do count as the variable being used. The warning in the OP is the variable was never **assigned** before being used, which is technically true.

The question is whether or not relying on the default value is okay or not. If so, then the warning don't have much use. Or at least not for built-in types, since their default is a valid value.

review_comments: What about enums? We should probably still recommend explicit initialization unlike `int`, since the enum value list does not necessarily start with or contain `0`.
Yeah, I agree with you. In this case it will show a warning, since enums have a different datatype kind.
